record.original_question: In the opaque-square barrier problem, if the barrier C is allowed to have n connected components instead of only one or two pieces, can one improve on the current best known length (2 + √3)/√2 · ℓ ≈ 2.639 · ℓ? Equivalently, does allowing arbitrarily many components keep lowering the achievable length so that the problem might have an infimum but no minimizing barrier?

evidence.quote: Si on autorise n morceaux pour C, peut-on améliorer encore la meilleure longueur obtenue ?

Au fond, peut-être qu’en autorisant n aussi grand que l’on veut, on peut toujours améliorer la solution... et le problème posé n’aurait pas de solution (une borne inférieure oui, mais pas de minimum).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be the closed unit square in the Euclidean plane, with side length $\ell>0$ (take $\ell=1$ for normalization). A subset $C\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is called an opaque barrier (or opaque set) for $S$ if $C$ is a finite union of rectifiable curves and every straight line in the plane that meets $S$ also meets $C$. The length $|C|$ is the sum of the one-dimensional Hausdorff measures of its components.

For an integer $n\ge 1$, let
$$L_n \;=\; \inf\bigl\{\,|C|\;:\; C \text{ is an opaque barrier for } S \text{ consisting of at most } n \text{ connected components}\bigr\}.$$
The shortest known opaque barrier (using two components: the Steiner tree of three vertices of $S$ together with a segment from the fourth vertex to the center) has length
$$\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\ell \;=\;\bigl(\sqrt{2}+\tfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\bigr)\ell \;\approx\; 2.6389\,\ell.$$

Questions:
(a) Does there exist an integer $n\ge 3$ and an opaque barrier for $S$ with at most $n$ connected components whose total length is strictly less than $\frac{2+\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\,\ell$?
(b) Is the sequence $(L_n)_{n\ge 1}$ strictly decreasing for all sufficiently large $n$, so that
$$L_\infty := \inf_{n\ge 1} L_n \;<\; L_n \quad\text{for every }n,$$
i.e., the infimum length over opaque barriers with finitely many components is not attained by any single barrier with a bounded number of components?
artifact.status_search_result: The opaque square problem remains open. The shortest known barrier for the unit square has length √2 + √6/2 ≈ 2.6389, known to be optimal only among barriers with at most two components; whether allowing more components yields shorter barriers is unresolved. The best general lower bound was recently improved from 2 (Jones, 1964) to roughly 2.00002, and no proof is known that a minimizer exists or that the conjectured value is optimal.

status_evidence.title: Opaque set - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The shortest known barrier has length √2 + √6/2 ≈ 2.6389. This is optimal among forests with only two components, and conjectured to be best possible more generally, but this remains unproven.
status_evidence.claim: The conjectured optimum 2.6389 is only proven optimal among 2-component barriers; the general case is open.

status_evidence.title: A lower bound on opaque sets
status_evidence.snippet: The total length of any countable family of rectifiable curves meeting every line through the unit square is at least 2.00002, the first improvement since 1964.
status_evidence.claim: The best known general lower bound is only ~2.00002, far below the conjectured 2.6389, indicating the problem is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Opaque Square (Dumitrescu-Jiang)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies short opaque sets for the unit square and discusses bounds for varying numbers of components.
status_evidence.claim: The component-count question for the opaque square is actively studied and remains open.
